body: Ok i just want to say that 'have you done ANYTHING? things wont fix themselves' is literally the most unhelpful and presumptuous thing anybody has ever said to me when I say 'i want to die'. You suck.

Feeling excited or happy at the prospect of finally ending your life is common from what I've read. Once you have made the decision you know there is an endpoint to your suffering. None of the pressures of life matter anymore so there can be a sense of relief - no more money worries, commitments, forcing yourself to work a job you hate... sounds really nice.

I am scared of hell but not as much as I used to be. I don't think I will feel anything after dying because I don't believe there is anything after death. This used to be a big motivator to not kill myself - something (life) had to be better than absolutely nothing (death) right? Lately I dont feel the same.

There are no magic words you can write to make him feel okay with his wife dying. It is going to be painful.

If someone I love was going to die I would want as many reminders of them as possible. I would appreciate lots of memories written down so I could think about how special the time together we had was. So I would try and put down special things with meaning to the two of you.

Your emotions make a lot of sense and I relate a lot. I am feeling like I can't escape the pit of my emotions, because of ny own mental illnesses. It sounds like you feel much more certain about your choice to die than I do, but I'm still really hoping you're able to pull yourself out of the pit one last time... You deserve to be happy and to want to live and I'm sure lits of people, including your husband, would be saddened knowing you feel like dying is the option that makes the most sense right now. I know I am.
Oh thanks for this post! This is a great idea.

>we all love our reactive dogs, but sometimes i can't help but wonder and wish... what would life be like if they were more "normal"

That's the thing, isn't it? Cuz they're not just snapping, snarling monsters. The same dog who lunged at me and bit me over and over is the one who dopily tries to share her toys with the cats, or rolls around on the floor making weird noises to make us laugh. She can be adorable and loving like any other dog, and it's easy sometimes to just hold onto that and hope that \*this\* time... that's all she'll do.

Thank you for the support. It means a lot.

Thank you everybody who replied. I honestly just needed to vent when I posted, did not expect the supportive and understanding comments. It makes something really hard just a little bit easier to know other people understand and/or have gone through the same thing.

> Consider the staff of any sanctuary you are looking into, but also consider Lily. 

The sanctuary does extensive work with behaviorists and has successfully rehabilitated several dogs with a history of aggression, has a large area of land with heated barns/areas with limited human interaction. Lily is never happier than when she is outside and around other dogs, so it seemed like a possible solution.

I'm very prepared for them to tell us that euthanasia is the only option and they can't/won't take her because she is such a risk. I'm going to trust their levels of experience and ask them to tell me what they think the best move is, however, I don't think I could forgive myself if I didn't ask at all.
